reviews.comment: Not a bad professor. Class content is incredibly easy. Attendance grade is absolutely ridiculous (-2% of final grade per absence), but outside of that it was a breeze. Professor cares far too much about "censorship" and made a huge spectacle out of it, so only take him if you are willing to be reminded of this every single lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Peterson teaches the material well and his lectures emphasize engagement. He really pushes people to think about their own beliefs, too. The class is much easier if you participate, and the larger assignments aren't super difficult especially if you put a little effort into them.

Hard class if you don't do the reading. That aside, he made me realize I love philosophy, and now I'm getting my minor because of his class. Teaches the material so well, and he is also extremely educated. Challenges you to think past your bias. Stands up for what he believes in, and we need more of that.
Very passionate about what he teaches. really engaging lectures with discussions.

Don't take this class. This is way harder than what an introductory philosophy class should be. The content isn't even terribly difficult to follow; it's just the way the class is set up. If you're looking for an A, sear away.

Philosophy as a subject is very difficult, but I really thought he had a great way at teaching it. You aren't graded by much (and there are 2 short essays), but I didn't find anything too hard, especially since there are recitations that are super helpful. If you are engaged, you should be fine!

Interesting class and a nice break away from STEM/engineering courses. 1 lecture for 75 minutes and 1 recitation for 90 minutes. The class is what you make of it. Points are deducted for missing more than 2 sessions of the lecture or recitation. Class is much more interesting when you actively participate. Nice and understanding professor for sure

Class ain't bad. Idk why I picked the 8AM lectures which made it harder to survive. Waiting for time to go by in rectiation and lecture is torture. Exams can be hard. Packback and online quiz due every week(easy to forget). All in all not bad. Nice break away from Math and Engineering.

Lots of assignments. Assignments due randomly at 8:00am. Mandatory attendance in class and recitation. Recitation is too long. Not that difficult but made difficult by being taught poorly. If you don't have a good TA you will have to spend a lot of time decoding whatever he says.

Really good professor and I got a good TA which definitely helped me. Assigned textbook reading with a couple questions each week, and then you have 2 exams and 2 essays. Some of the exam questions are tricky because they're worded weirdly, but the essays are straightforward. Just study really well the night before the exam and you're good to go.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is a great prof! Yes, attendance is mandatory, but he has a little bit of leniency, which is nice. If you do go to class, he is funny and will often make it worth your while with interesting conversations. Weekly homework, but it's not hard. The only thing I disliked about his class was my TA, but that's not his fault.

Should be easier. I took this class thinking it would be an easy A compared to the 3 other upper-level math classes I am in, but this is probably the only class I do not get an A in. TAs grade very hard on papers and projects. The recitations and homework are boring and not helpful. Tests are difficult to score highly on. Prof decent class is bad.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is a nice guy and overall good lecturer but the class overall is unnecessarily difficult for it being a level 100 core credit class. The TA's grade ridiculously strict and have a ton of bias towards papers and the group presentation. Recitations are a waste of time and everything is mandatory attendance.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade made up of papers, exams, and weekly mindtap homework (as well as one group project). The papers and weekly homework are relatively easy, but the exams are worded ambiguously and will confuse you. Peterson's Canvas is also extremely unorganized. Take another professor if possible.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. If you can, take the other philosophy 111 professor. His lectures were hard to understand and lengthy. His exams were pretty difficult but as long as you study you should be fine. The absolute worst part of this class were the recitations and TAs. The TAs graded the essays you write in the class and they grade tough.

He is nice but has an accent and is hard to understand. The lectures are boring and attendance counts towards your grade. There are only two exams which can be tricky and you have to do a lot of reading and studying. There are two easily graded short essays and weekly assignments that also require a good amount of work. Fine but not recommended

If you're a STEM major or need PHIL 111 as a prereq, DO NOT take him. He has a heavy accent that makes it hard to understand him, and he has very few things that he grades you by. If you just need this course for some liberal arts credit and don't care about philosophy, take someone else!!

You seriously need to show up to this class. Attendance is a grade and also matters. All slides are posted on Canvas. The exams were difficult and it caused him to throw out some questions and gave a curve. Whole class time is lecture. Do not miss the Friday classes. He is a cool professor but I did not like the class. Would not take again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is a great guy! He tries his best to make difficult topics easier to understand. The class was tough, and the exams were worth 25% each, but he offers 5% extra credit and curves every exam. Definitely NOT a "blow off" class, but definitely manageable if you listen and go to lecture. Uses iclicker to take attendance.

I primarily choose this class because it double counted for University Core Curriculum. However, by the end of the semester I ended up liking it. Dr. Peterson is transparent about grades and expectations. The lectures are interesting and they open you up to new ways of thinking. As a freshman engineering student the workload is very manageable.
Professor Peterson is awesome. He is a great lecturer and engages with the class. Papers are easy and you only have 2 tests. Weekly homework which is also super easy.

He is very engaging with the lecture material. He allows students to share diverse thoughts and opinions, and some of the discussions are very interesting. Also his accent is awesome. 10/10 would take again.

He was very nice and knew what he was talking about but it was very hard to understand with his accent. The slides didn't make much sense and the TA was very strict. Recitation is where I learned most of it. The tests were ridiculously hard. I thought it would be an easy blowoff elective but this ended up being my lowest grade this semester.

Dr. Peterson is a good professor, but it is very hard to keep up with him during his lectures. Everything I learned in the course was due to recitation and my friends. Wouldn't suggest him because there are other options, but it is possible to get an A and you only have one assignment a week plus two short papers and a few tests.

Dr. Peterson is a pretty good professor, but if you can take someone else, I would. His class is interesting, but way too much work for what it is. Attendance is mandatory and you can only miss three classes before you lose points. He gives weekly assignments that can be time-consuming and his exams are way too hard and misleading.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The professor himself was not bad, he obviously knew what he was talking about. The only thing was the lectures were sort of confusing for me, most of the time I had to watch youtube vids or wait until recitation to get a better understanding. Thankfully extra credit was given when needed. Overall experience: 5.5/10

This class is lecture heavy, and the homework assignments are easy. All notes are provided on Canvas, and Mr. Peterson is hilarious and easy to approach. Tests are SO easy if you write down weekly objectives, and make reviews for the two exams. Two papers are also very easy. This class is interesting, outside of the box, and super energetic.

This class has a midterm and a final, weekly homework, and two papers. Overall it's a very interesting class because he challenges your own beliefs but in a respectful way. The tests are pretty difficult because they are very conceptual questions. Study the textbook and the TA's class more than the lecture slides.

This class was very interesting and you need to be ready to talk about taboo topics. He loves having the class engage in discussions and is very good at challenging everyone's personal views. The recitations are very important to make sure you fully understand some complex topics! Pay attention and you'll do well. 2 exams, weekly homework.

In class was purely discussion based and the exams are exact opposite with very unclear and confusing questions. Homework was easy but did not help prepare at all for the exams. There are 2 essays but the TAs grade them and are very biased and grade with their opinion solely. Such a stressful class for no reason, DO NOT TAKE.

class does not at all prepare you for tests on your own to figure it out. HW is easy, papers are easy to get a good grade on but hard to offset test with. Have to go to class its a grade, hopefully you get Michael as ur TA he's the best. Overall not an amazing class, you think you have an A until you dont

Martin has a very thick accent that is often very hard to understand in a large, echoey lecture hall. Recitation was much more helpful than class. Grades consisted of weekly assignments (took around 15-30 minutes and are the best study tools for exams), 2 essays (400 word and 1000 word), and 2 exams. Final is not cumulative. Takes attendance.

Professor Peterson is a good professor but his lectures can become confusing sometimes. The homework and 2 essays are very easy, but the 2 exams are difficult and the questions are a tad confusing. Overall, a good class.

The homework is super easy, 2 essays throughout the semester and one group project. Prof Peterson was a good lecturer, but sometimes it would just get boring and hard to pay attention to. The tests are also randomly pretty hard, not at all like the fill in the blank homeworks.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took him for seminar, and it was one of my favorite classes ever. I loved his style. It was discussion based, and he would always challenge us in our positions and arguments, but then make sure we don't give in too easily. He didn't like if we agreed with him too quickly (in a fun way). Grade was based on writing papers and presenting them.
